relationship: Running either path-search algorithm on the same editable road map connects frontier priority rules to route exploration.

learnerLoop.action: Choose Dijkstra or A*, adjust a road cost if needed, and run the search.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The frontier, settled towns and route decisions advance.
learnerLoop.evidence: The graph, priority explanation, progress and settled order show the search.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Compare the next town chosen and explain the effect of the heuristic.

invariants: Both algorithms operate on the displayed road network and costs.
The settled order and frontier evidence follow the selected algorithm's priority rule.
safeAdaptations: Change map stories, costs or prompts while retaining a comparable Dijkstra and A* trace.
nonGoals: Offering arbitrary graph algorithms beyond the two displayed searches.

task.description: Current problem statement and supplied quantities.
task.visibility: Shown at the start of each problem or stage.

model.description: Operated construction and its live measurements; see quantities for what is given and revealed.
model.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

working.description: Ordered calculations, learner entries and consequential evidence for the current task.
working.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

completion.description: Achievement, next task or learning transition.
completion.visibility: Shown only when the local completion conditions below are satisfied; representation controls are separately identified.

feedback.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

cost-editor.description: Adjust a selected edge after both algorithm challenges.
cost-editor.visibility: Hidden until editing is unlocked and an edge cost is selected.

algorithm.description: Algorithm selection, conditional reveal and experiment reset.
algorithm.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

road-costs.description: Positive weighted edges and the fixed heuristic are supplied evidence.
road-costs.domain: Numeric road costs and heuristic estimates; no physical units.
road-costs.source: Initial costs and h values are given; after both searches finish, learner may edit road costs.
road-costs.output: Costs remain on the map; the editor uses decrement/increment buttons.

next-frontier-node.description: Choose the next minimum-priority town. Tied minima are alternative valid values of this ONE decision.
next-frontier-node.domain: Town IDs in the current frontier.
next-frontier-node.source: Learner chooses using g for Dijkstra or g+h for A*.
next-frontier-node.output: Wrong choices stay in the frontier with feedback; a legal choice settles the town and reveals each relaxation.

route-and-cost.description: The completed predecessor route, total cost and settled order are computed outputs.
route-and-cost.domain: Ordered node list plus numeric total and counts.
route-and-cost.source: Built from accepted search decisions and relaxations, not entered into answer boxes.
route-and-cost.output: Comparison cards appear after each algorithm reaches the goal; both enable cost experiments.

modes.algorithm: Dijkstra is selected and started initially. The algorithm toggle starts a fresh Dijkstra or A* search; stored comparison results are kept for the same road costs.
modes.support: There is no None/Some/All setting. A wrong frontier choice makes Reveal minimum available. A* displays g, h and f; Dijkstra uses g.

dependencies: Only frontier nodes can be chosen; busy relaxation animation temporarily blocks choices.
Accepting a minimum settles it and relaxes its neighbours; selecting G at minimum priority fixes the route.
Both algorithms must finish before cost editing unlocks. Changing costs invalidates/restarts current experiments as implemented.
implementation.completion: finishSearch() runs when G is settled as a minimum. Each algorithm stores route, cost, settled list and tie choices; both results unlock road-cost editing.
limitations: There are no numerical answer fields. Route cost and relaxation values are shown evidence, not learner-produced numeric unknowns.
